whoWeAre.title: Who We Are
whoWeAre.metaDescription: The founding story, team, legal identity and governance of Samma färger, a Swedish foundation funding programmes for children affected by the war in Ukraine.
whoWeAre.heroTitle: We started at a kitchen table in Malmö. We're still run the same way.
whoWeAre.storyIntro: In first person, from co-founder Elin Håkansson:
storyParagraphs: In March 2022 I was coordinating logistics for a Red Cross chapter in Skåne, watching convoys of donated goods leave Sweden with almost no visibility into what happened to them after the border. Friends kept asking where to send money instead — and I didn't have a good answer.

Marcus, who audited small nonprofits for a living, and I started keeping a shared spreadsheet: what we'd raised, who received it, what it bought. We showed it to the first twenty donors unedited. Nobody unsubscribed.

By late 2022 we'd registered as a foundation and set up our first standing partnership, with a small education charity in Dnipro run by people who'd been doing this work long before we existed. That relationship — local partners leading delivery, us funding and reporting — is still the model today.
We're not the largest organisation working on this. We're trying to be one of the most legible: you should be able to look at any number on this site and find out exactly where it came from.
whoWeAre.teamIntro: Six people across two countries, plus the local partner staff who do most of the actual delivery work.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.metaDescription: The problem we work on, our four programme pillars, where we work in Ukraine, and the principles that govern every partnership.
mission.heroTitle: The war didn't pause childhood. Neither should the response.
mission.pillarsIntro: Each pillar is delivered by a local partner organisation we fund and monitor — we do not run direct-delivery teams for these programmes ourselves.

pillars.title: Education continuity
pillars.what: School kits, replacement stationery, and small grants to schools for heating and repair so classrooms can reopen sooner.
pillars.how: Needs are identified jointly with school administrators; kits are packed regionally and distributed at the school or a community centre.
pillars.who: Delivered by four regional partner organisations, coordinated by our Programme Director in Dnipro.
pillars.cost: Roughly 250 kr per child per term for a standard kit; larger school-repair grants are assessed individually and require three competing quotes.

pillars.title: Shelter & safety
pillars.what: Weatherproofing and basic equipping of shared basement shelters used during air-raid alerts.
pillars.how: Sites are prioritised using housing-administration data on families with young children, then insulated, lit, and stocked with first aid supplies.
pillars.who: Delivered with municipal facilities staff and our Kharkiv-based field coordinator.
pillars.cost: Roughly 2,000 kr per shelter for a full weatherproofing kit.

pillars.title: Psychosocial support
pillars.what: Structured, supervised play and group sessions for children, run by trained local facilitators.
pillars.how: Sessions run several afternoons a week in renovated courtyard spaces or community centres; no counting or press access during sessions.
pillars.who: Delivered by the Dnipro Children's Fund and two smaller partners in Zaporizhzhia and Lviv.
pillars.cost: Roughly 750 kr funds one week of sessions for a group of eight children.

pillars.title: Nutrition
pillars.what: Daily hot meals prepared and distributed through community-run kitchens.
pillars.how: Kitchens purchase ingredients locally under our procurement policy and report meal counts weekly.
pillars.who: Delivered by the Kharkiv Relief Kitchen Network and partner kitchens in Kherson and Chernihiv.
pillars.cost: Roughly 9 kr per meal, including preparation and distribution.

mission.principlesIntro: These four commitments apply to every partnership, every campaign, and every piece of content we publish.

principles.title: Child safeguarding first
principles.desc: No child is named, geo-located, or photographed without recorded guardian consent. Every field staff member signs our code of conduct before contact with children.

principles.title: Local partnership, not parallel delivery
principles.desc: We fund and monitor local organisations rather than sending Sweden-based staff to deliver programmes directly. They know the context; we bring funding discipline and reporting.

principles.title: No duplication of aid
principles.desc: Before funding a new site, we check regional coordination lists to avoid delivering where another organisation already covers the same need.

principles.title: Dignity of recipients
principles.desc: Families are never required to be photographed, tell their story, or prove hardship beyond what a local partner's intake process already establishes.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.metaDescription: Where every krona goes, our overhead ratio explained, procurement policy, safeguarding policy, and how to raise a complaint.
transparency.heroEyebrow: Read before you give, not after
transparency.allocationBody: 83% of every krona goes directly to programme delivery — school kits, shelter materials, meals, and psychosocial facilitator salaries paid to local partners. 9% covers administration: audit, insurance, financial systems and core staff not tied to a single programme. 8% covers fundraising: payment processing fees, campaign materials, and donor communications. We publish this split every quarter, not just annually, and it is cross-checked against our audited accounts.
transparency.overheadTitle: Why we don't chase a 'zero overhead' claim
transparency.overheadBody: Some organisations advertise that '100% of your donation reaches the field' by having a separate fund cover salaries and audit costs. We don't do that — it just moves the same costs off the page. Our 9% administration figure is the real, audited cost of running this organisation responsibly, including the audit that lets you verify every other number on this site.
transparency.procurementBody: Purchases above 15,000 SEK require three competing quotes, documented in our finance system. We prioritise Ukrainian suppliers for goods available locally, both to support the local economy and to reduce cross-border logistics risk. No board member, staff member or their immediate family may hold a financial interest in a supplier we use.
transparency.safeguardingBody: Every staff member and long-term volunteer with any contact with children completes a safeguarding briefing and signs our code of conduct before starting. No child is identified by full name, school, or precise address in any published material. Every identifiable photograph of a child requires written guardian consent, recorded separately from the photograph itself. Concerns can be raised confidentially — see the complaints section below.
transparency.complaintsBody: If something about our fundraising, a programme, or the conduct of any staff member or partner concerns you, contact complaints@sammafarger.example directly, or use the contact form and select 'Complaint'. We acknowledge every complaint within two business days and a board member reviews any safeguarding-related complaint personally.
transparency.reportsIntro: Annual reports and audit statements, most recent first.
transparency.privacyBody: We collect only what we need: your contact details if you donate or subscribe, and — only after you actively consent via the cookie banner — privacy-respecting, non-tracking analytics on which pages are used. We never sell or share personal data with third parties for marketing. Payment card details are handled entirely by Stripe and PayPal; we never see or store them. You can request a copy of, correction to, or deletion of your data at any time by emailing privacy@sammafarger.example, in line with the EU GDPR and the Swedish Data Protection Act.
